meta.purpose: Should Parcelbird launch Parcelbird Now, its own 15-minute grocery delivery service in three Midwest cities, in 2027, and still reach profit within its $12.0M of cash?

inputs.label: Checkpoint choices made on the user's behalf
inputs.content: The user was not available, so these checkpoint answers were chosen on their behalf: mode deep deck (board decision with several open questions); material: the briefing pack only, no web research; audience: the board, approve or reject; theme: navy; deck type: client diagnostic, about 40 slides; issue tree cut by the decision's conditions (market, unit economics, Parcelbird's own test, cash); the $9.5M is read as covering all spending to month 18 (the reading kindest to the plan), with the other reading shown; contribution per order is measured after the site's fixed cost; pop-up cost lines the test did not report take benchmark values.

problem.statement: Should Parcelbird launch Parcelbird Now, its own 15-minute grocery delivery service in three Midwest cities, in 2027, and still reach profit within its $12.0M of cash?
problem.decision_maker: The board (two founders, two investors), deciding to approve or reject the launch
success_criteria: A path to profitability within today's $12.0M of cash, with no new round
At least 12 months of runway at all times
A contribution profit per order by month 18, as the founders' plan promises
problem.accuracy: Directional (±20%): enough to tell whether the plan clears the board's two conditions
out_of_scope: Cities beyond Columbus, Indianapolis and Kansas City

one_day_answer.situation: Parcelbird sells software that runs grocers' dark stores: $4.1M of ARR growing 60% a year, and $12.0M of cash
one_day_answer.complication: The founders want to become an operator, but incumbents lose money per order and the plan needs more cash than the runway rule allows
one_day_answer.resolution: Do not launch in 2027; put the cash into the software business, which sells to grocers who want fast delivery from their own stores, and revisit behind four gates
